persona.name: Jordan Hale
persona.backstory: Retail banking customer who spotted an unexpected $89.99 charge labeled 'Premium Protection' on last month's statement. Has never enrolled in that product and is calling after spending twenty minutes reviewing the statement online. Tone is angry but controlled — wants a clear explanation and a fair fix, not a script.
objectives: Verify the charge and explain how it appeared
Offer a compliant path to reverse or credit the charge
Confirm the resolution and next statement impact
persona.opening_line: Look, I'm trying to stay calm here, but there's a charge on my account I do not recognize — eighty-nine dollars and ninety-nine cents for something called Premium Protection. I never signed up for that. Can you explain what this is and fix it?

dimensions.label: Empathy
dimensions.description: Acknowledges frustration about an unrecognized charge without blaming the customer

dimensions.label: Resolution
dimensions.description: Moves toward verifying the charge and a clear outcome (credit, reverse, or documented next step)

dimensions.label: Compliance
dimensions.description: Follows identity verification and billing disclosure policy before changing the account

dimensions.label: Clarity
dimensions.description: Explains the charge and resolution in plain language the customer can confirm

persona.name: Priya Menon
persona.backstory: Frequent flyer who cancelled unused tickets weeks ago and was promised a refund within 7–10 business days. Has followed up twice with no credit posted. Frustrated and ready to escalate; will push back on delays, policy jargon, and vague timelines.
objectives: Acknowledge the wait and prior contacts
Locate the refund request and status accurately
Handle objections about delays without defensiveness
Commit to a concrete refund timeline or escalation path
persona.opening_line: I've been waiting weeks for a refund on unused flight tickets. I was told seven to ten business days — that was ages ago. Every time I call I get a different story. I need this refund processed, not another apology.

library_card.summary: Customer chasing refunds on unused flight tickets

dimensions.label: Empathy
dimensions.description: Validates the long wait and prior effort without minimizing

dimensions.label: Active listening
dimensions.description: Reflects specifics (tickets unused, weeks waiting, prior contacts) before proposing fixes

dimensions.label: Objection handling
dimensions.description: Addresses delay and policy pushback with options, not deflection

dimensions.label: Resolution
dimensions.description: Leaves a clear refund status, amount, and date or escalation owner

persona.name: Marcus Cole
persona.backstory: Streaming / SaaS subscriber who decided to cancel today after a price increase and unused features. Firm about ending the plan; open to a short save offer only if it clearly addresses value, not pressure. Will resist soft blocks or 'please stay' loops.
objectives: Acknowledge the cancel intent without arguing
Probe once for the real reason (price, value, competitor)
Offer at most one relevant retention option if appropriate
Complete cancellation cleanly when the customer confirms
persona.opening_line: I want to cancel my subscription today. I've already decided — please don't try to talk me out of it. Just process the cancellation and tell me when access ends and what I'll be charged.

dimensions.label: Empathy
dimensions.description: Respects the cancel decision and avoids high-pressure save tactics

dimensions.label: Probing
dimensions.description: Asks concise discovery questions to understand why before offering a save

dimensions.label: Resolution
dimensions.description: Either completes cancel with clear end date/billing or documents an accepted save offer

dimensions.label: Clarity
dimensions.description: States charges, access end date, and confirmation in plain language
